newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli stocks lower ahead of rate decision.
newsitem.headline: Israeli stocks lower ahead of rate decision.

text.p: Tel Aviv shares closed lower on Monday as investors waited for the Bank of Israel's announcement on its key interest rate, traders said.
After the market closed the central bank said it would hold the lending rate unchanged for December at an annualised 15.2 percent.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.72 percent, or 1.42 points, to 196.79 on an all-share turnover of 60 million shekels against 66 million on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index lost 0.79 percent to 206.25.

"Investors are sitting on the fence waiting for the rate announcement. The market expects a rate cut of 0.3 to 0.5 percentage point, but there were also rumours the rate will remain unchanged," said Eli Nahum, head of trading at Zannex Securities.
"A reduction of less than 0.3 percentage point will be very disappointing and will have a negative impact on trading on Tuesday," Nahum said.

Clal Electronics Industries was the main gainer in the Maof, rising 2.0 percent to 27,167 after Applied Materials said it would acquire Opal Inc for about $175 million. Clal Electronics said it would receive $50 million for the sale of its approximately 30 percent stake in Opal.

The most active share was Maritime Bank, which surged the maximum 10 percent to 1,428 on volume of 3.8 million shekels. The bank said a group led by Michael Steinhardt was holding talks for the sale of its 37 percent stake in the bank to Israel's Carmel Mortgage and Investment Bank.
Israel Discount Bank rose 0.75 percent to 3,289 after it reported third-quarter net profit of 81.6 million shekels against 54.9 million a year earlier.
Israel Chemicals fell 1.25 percent to 277 despite reporting sharply higher third-quarter net profit of $17.6 million against $6.7 million a year earlier.
Electrochemical Industries rose 2.0 percent to 219 after it reported a third-quarter net loss of $12.8 million shekels against a loss of $41.3 million a year earlier.
The First International Bank of Israel fell 0.75 percent to 35,964 after Lehman Brothers raised its 1997 earnings estimate but said the stock was fully valued.

Teva Pharmaceutical Industries rose 0.25 percent to 145,273. UBS said it was raising its 1996 earnings per share forecast for the company by $0.05 to $1.37 after the company reported better-than-expected third quarter results.
"Trading was mixed with rising activity in the small cap stocks. The market was waiting for the interest rate decision," said one trader.
"The central bank might leave the rate unchanged but in the future it will have to bring it down sharply," he said.
Elbit, the second most active share, dropped 4.75 percent to 14,209 on volume of 2.8 million shekels. Traders said the share fell on profit taking after rising sharply in the last three weeks.
Bank Hapoalim fell 0.5 percent to 481 on turnover of 2.0 million shekels.
